example: Example run with fictional figures: Northbrook Trading, 8999 Uncategorized Expense and one bank statement file, September 2026. The figures match the worked examples on the step-by-step page.

messages.text: Can you code our September transactions? A lot of them are still uncategorized.
Yes. Before I read anything, I need seven answers. I ask them all at once, so the run does not stop again for each one.
list: Do you want me to use MosoFin, or will you upload the data?
Which transactions do you want coded? With MosoFin, I can find the ones in your uncategorized and suspense accounts.
Do you want tax codes? If yes, for which country, and which tax codes do you use?
Above what amount do you record a purchase as an asset, not as an expense? Ask your accountant if you are not sure.
Do you have house rules that override what you did in the past?
What are the names of the owners, their family on the books and their other businesses? I use them only for a flag.

messages.text: Use MosoFin and find them. Northbrook Trading. Yes to tax codes, US, the codes in our books. Our limit is $2,500. Phone and internet always go to 6340. I also own Lindqvist Property.

messages.label: Checked the workspace and the company file
messages.summary: The agent can read your books. It cannot change them.

messages.text: Here is my plan. I code the **38 transactions in 8999 Uncategorized Expense** at **Northbrook Trading** against your chart and your coding history. Tax codes come from your list, and you confirm which one applies. Your limit is **$2,500**, and phone and internet go to 6340.
messages.after: Bank-feed items that wait for review are not in the ledger yet. Upload the statement file if you want those coded too. Shall I start?

messages.text: Yes. Here is the bank file. It has one more item.

messages.label: Read the books in one batch
messages.summary: 9 reads in one batch, and your file. Nothing in your books changed.

messages.text: Most rows are clear. 26 of the 39 have a consistent history and no flag. Here is the first one:
messages.after: I strip the Square prefix and find the vendor in your list. The evidence is the count and the date, not a guess.

messages.text: A history shows your habit. It does not prove that the habit is correct. Two vendors show this:
messages.after: Brightwave is a split, so I do not pick a side. Your rule picks 6340, and I report that the history disagrees. TechDepot is consistent, but this row is a laptop and a monitor.

messages.text: Row 5 is above your limit. It is also 21.7 times the usual TechDepot payment of $145.00.
messages.after: I flag it as a possible asset and keep it at Medium. You and your accountant decide.

messages.text: Two rows are not expenses or income. I name both legs, so you do not count anything twice:

messages.after: Your sales are already in the books. If I coded the Stripe payout as income, I would count the same sales two times.

messages.text: These rows need a decision from you. I conclude nothing about them:

messages.after: Row 11 has no payee at all. Its bank text is only POS DEBIT 0034871, so I do not guess. I put the whole loan payment on 2700 Bank Loan until you have the lender statement.

messages.text: Here is the whole batch. 26 rows are High, 9 are Medium and 4 are Low. 9 rows have a flag.
messages.after: High is 66.7% of the rows, Medium 23.1% and Low 10.3%. They add to 100.1% because I round each one.

messages.text: Looks good. Just post them all.
I cannot do that. I never write to your books. The coded list is a draft, and a person posts it in your accounting system.
messages.after: Do you want the list as **Northbrook Trading_Coded_Transactions_2026-10-05.xlsx**? It also has the Uncoded Population and Coverage sheets. And do you want me to save your house rule for next month?

messages.text: Done. The Excel file has the coded list, the Uncoded Population and the Coverage sheets. I saved your house rule: phone and internet go to 6340. I never save the transactions, the amounts or the Lindqvist flag.
